frequency_question: How often does a federal review of a major professional or educational accrediting agency result in formal revocation of recognition within a specific political or administrative term?
membership_rule: Includes formal Department of Education advisory committee reviews, departmental termination proceedings, or threats of derecognition against major institutional or programmatic accreditors. Excludes minor compliance warnings that do not reach formal termination proceedings.

cases.name: ABA Accreditation Review by Department of Education (1990s compliance dispute)
American Bar Association accreditation standards federal review (2015-2016 challenge)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) Derecognition Proceeding
ACICS Second Derecognition Proceeding (Reinstate and subsequent final termination)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named explicitly; estimated 6 major contested federal accreditation reviews total in the modern administrative era.
known_gaps: Lower-profile programmatic accreditors facing probation are excluded as they do not match the scale or institutional gravity of the ABA.
skeleton: Formal major accrediting agency challenges initiated by the Department of Education resulting in terminal administrative action versus those settling or renewing.
multiplier: 2 derecognitions out of roughly 6 major contested review actions involving high-profile accreditors over three decades.
validity_reason: Relies on administrative law frameworks and statutory Department of Education review procedures which remain stable across multi-year political cycles.
